chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic
The adulterer maries not except an adulteress or a polytheess

He said: They were men and women who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) known for adultery, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade [marrying] those men and women; and the people today are upon that status, whoever publicized any of that or a legal penalty was established upon him, do not marry him until his repentance is recognized.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for marrying someone who is known for adultery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Quranic prohibition in Surah An-Nur (24:3) specifically targets those notorious for adultery during the Prophet's era, establishing a precedent for public notoriety (shuhrat). This ruling extends to contemporary individuals who are publicly known for such acts or have undergone the legal penalty, prohibiting their marriage until genuine repentance is recognized and verified by the community.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic
[24:3] And the adulterer shall not marry any but a adulteress or an idolatress

, heasws said: ‘These were the men and the women in the era of Rasool-Allahsaww notorious with the adultery. So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Forbade from those men and the women; and the people today are upon that status, the one who has been publicised with anything from that, or a legal Penalty (Hadd) has been established upon him. Therefore, do not marry him until you recognise his repentance’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla’ ibn Muhammad al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the word of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious,
‘A prostitute man cannot marry but a prostitute woman or a pagan,’ [24:4]

has said, ‘During the time of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, there were well-known prostitutes female and male. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has prohibited forming marriage contract with such men and women. Today people who become known as such or are convicted for fornication and punished (by the qualified court) are of the same status. No one must marry them unless it is known that they have repented.’”
